correctness.rationale: Use Shor Proposition 3.4 for the exact gap set. For a=g+1 the semigroup is ordinary; for a=2 its positive elements are all evens and sufficiently large odds, each Arf. When q≥1,a≥3, each omitted high gap h=g+ka is produced by the legitimate first-step triple (h−1,h−1,h−2); the proposed oversemigroup T is Arf because triples with largest element >g stay in its conductor tail and all smaller selected elements are multiples of a. This gives A(S)=T, genus g−q and conductor g+1. Independent direct finite all-triple operator and fixed-point tests verified 263 admissible (g,a) pairs with g≤25, 226 nontrivial; unrestricted proof is the gap argument.
